Melos stood before the ruler. He was only a shepherd, but he was not afraid.
"You kill people without asking if they did anything wrong!"
he shouted.
"My guards will kill you too,"
said the ruler. Melos thought of his sister. Her wedding was tomorrow.
"Give me three days,"
he said.
"I promise to return." "What if you run away?"
His friend stepped forward.
"Keep me here. I trust him."
The ruler smiled.
"If you are not back by sunset on the third day, your friend will die."
Melos looked at his friend.
"I will wait,"

his friend said. After the wedding, Melos started back. Rain fell hard all night. By morning, dark water covered the bridge. He could not wait. His friend's life depended on him. Melos jumped into the river. The water pulled him under. He fought to reach the other side. At last, he caught a tree branch and pulled himself out. Cold and wet, he ran on. Three men blocked the road.
"Give us your money!" "I have none!"
One man hit him with a stick. Melos pushed past him and ran. The men shouted behind him. Soon his legs shook. He could hardly move. He fell beside the road.
The sun was low. He could rest here. He could stay alive. But his friend would die.
"Why did I make that promise?"
he whispered. He closed his eyes. For a moment, he wanted to forget everything. Then he remembered his friend's face.
"I will wait."

Melos opened his eyes. Water ran between some stones nearby. He drank and slowly stood up. His friend was still waiting. He began to run again. When he reached the city square, a guard was lifting his sword. His friend stood with his hands tied.
"Stop!"
Melos cried.
"I'm here!"
He fell at his friend's feet.
"I almost left you,"
he said. His friend bent down.
"But you came back."
The ruler stared at them. For a moment, no one spoke.
"Let them both go,"
he said at last.
"I thought no one could trust another person so much."
The guard cut the ropes. Melos took his friend's hand. This time, they left together.
